claims.claim: Nucor's structural chain is recycled/raw steel inputs -> electric-arc-furnace and downstream fabrication capacity -> construction/manufacturing/energy infrastructure -> durable physical-system needs; liquidity supports capacity optionality but does not itself establish project returns.

EAF scale can reduce dependence on integrated blast-furnace routes, but successor bottlenecks include scrap quality/availability, electricity, qualified capacity, trade conditions and end-market utilization.

risks.risk: Physical steel demand is durable, but company returns remain sensitive to spreads, utilization and capital discipline on new capacity.

unknowns.unknown: Project-level returns on new capacity and adjacent technology investments remain unproven in current evidence.

claims.claim: Q2 adjusted EPS exceeded June guidance, supporting near-term execution credibility, but the reported EPS uplift from the Helion mark is non-operating and should not be used as evidence of core steel execution.

Strong liquidity reduces financing fragility, yet cyclicality and capital intensity remain the central falsifiers: new capacity can destroy value if spreads/utilization weaken or if trade support changes.

risks.risk: Steel spreads and utilization can reverse quickly with construction/manufacturing cycles and trade-policy changes.
Non-operating investment marks can inflate reported earnings and confidence if not separated from core operating performance.

contradictions.claim: Reported EPS includes a favorable Helion mark while adjusted EPS excludes it.
contradictions.resolution: Use adjusted EPS and operating EBITDA for core execution; treat Helion as separate optionality rather than steel earnings.

unknowns.unknown: Durability of above-guidance earnings requires subsequent-quarter evidence.
